sentences.zh: 你好，我是安德鲁·罗斯-索尔金。

sentences.zh: 我为《纽约时报》的每日通讯 DealBook 报道商业和政策新闻。

sentences.en: So there was this one time that I almost blew up a cabin.
sentences.zh: 有一次，我差点把一间小屋炸了。

sentences.en: It was 2009 and I was visiting my sister in Chile and we'd rented a cabin in the mountains to go hiking.
sentences.zh: 那是2009年，我去智利看望我姐姐，我们租了一间山里的小屋去徒步旅行。

sentences.en: I thought I was cooking onions.
sentences.zh: 我以为我在炒洋葱。

sentences.en: I was standing there by the stove and I started coughing a lot and that's when I noticed that the onions weren't cooking and realized that I hadn't actually lit the stove.
sentences.zh: 我站在炉子旁，开始剧烈咳嗽，就在那时我注意到洋葱根本没在煮，才意识到我其实根本没点火。

sentences.en: I looked around.
sentences.zh: 我环顾四周。

sentences.en: I found some matches.
sentences.zh: 我找到了一些火柴。

sentences.en: I was just about to light it when my sister came running into the house screaming at me to tell me that she could smell what I couldn't, which was that I had
sentences.zh: 我正要点火时，我姐姐冲进屋里对我尖叫，告诉我她闻到了我闻不到的东西，那就是我

sentences.en: accidentally filled the whole cabin with propane gas.
sentences.zh: 不小心让整个小屋都充满了丙烷气体。

sentences.en: My name is Brooke Jarvis and I'm a contributing writer for the New York Times magazine.
sentences.zh: 我叫布鲁克·贾维斯，是《纽约时报》杂志的特约撰稿人。

sentences.en: And for this week, I wrote a story about the coronavirus and smell, since loss of smell is one of the strangest symptoms of the virus.
sentences.zh: 本周，我写了一篇关于新冠病毒与嗅觉的故事，因为嗅觉丧失是该病毒最奇怪的症状之一。

sentences.en: I don't have a functioning sense of smell.
sentences.zh: 我的嗅觉功能不正常。

sentences.en: I don't ever remember having a sense of smell.
sentences.zh: 我不记得自己曾经有过嗅觉。

sentences.en: I don't know what it means really to smell something except by watching the people around me react to smells.
sentences.zh: 我并不真正知道闻东西是什么感觉，只能通过观察周围人对气味的反应来了解。

sentences.en: I don't notice when something is fishy.
sentences.zh: 我闻不出东西是不是坏了。

sentences.en: I don't notice if somebody has farted.
sentences.zh: 我闻不出别人是不是放了屁。

sentences.en: And every person that
sentences.zh: 而且每一个

sentences.en: I've ever lived with has been kind enough to allow me to ask them over and over again to smell the armpits of my sweaters to let me know if they need to be washed.
sentences.zh: 和我住在一起的人，都好心地允许我反复请求他们闻闻我毛衣的腋下，告诉我是否需要清洗。

sentences.en: It's something that I'm very used to and I don't stress about it.
sentences.zh: 我已经习惯了，对此并不感到压力。

sentences.en: But I have also started taking a propane detector with me sometimes when I travel.
sentences.zh: 但我旅行时有时也会随身携带一个丙烷探测器。

sentences.en: Compared to our other senses that we've understood the basics of them, things like hearing and
sentences.zh: 与其他我们已经掌握了基本原理的感官（比如听觉和

sentences.en: vision for decades or centuries even, smell is something that we're only beginning to understand.
sentences.zh: 视觉，甚至已经研究了几十年甚至几个世纪）相比，嗅觉是我们才刚刚开始了解的东西。

sentences.en: The receptors that allow us to perceive odors weren't discovered until the 1990s.
sentences.zh: 直到20世纪90年代，我们才发现了能够感知气味的受体。

sentences.en: For years now, I've had a Google alert set for anosmia, which is the scientific term for not being able to smell.
sentences.zh: 多年来，我一直为“嗅觉缺失症”（anosmia，即无法闻到气味的科学术语）设置了谷歌提醒。

sentences.en: And this spring, that alert, which is usually fairly quiet, started going off multiple times a day as science began to notice this unusual symptom associated with COVID.
sentences.zh: 而今年春天，这个通常相当安静的提醒开始每天响好几次，因为科学界开始注意到这种与新冠病毒相关的异常症状。

sentences.en: Scientists actually realized very early on that not only was it a symptom, it was the best indicator
sentences.zh: 科学家们其实很早就意识到，这不仅是一种症状，还是一个人

sentences.en: that somebody had been exposed to the coronavirus, even though what we were actually doing was screening people for coughs and high fevers.
sentences.zh: 是否接触过新冠病毒的最佳指标，尽管我们当时实际上是在筛查咳嗽和高烧患者。

sentences.en: But the people who really were talking about smell the most are the ones who lost it after being infected with the virus.
sentences.zh: 但真正谈论嗅觉最多的人，是那些在感染病毒后失去嗅觉的人。

sentences.en: For those people, it was a shocking discovery that smell was a much bigger part of their lives than they had ever realized before.
sentences.zh: 对这些人来说，这是一个令人震惊的发现：嗅觉在他们生活中所占的比重远比他们之前意识到的要大得多。

sentences.en: People said that it was like living their lives in black and white or living behind a sheet of glass, and they no longer felt like they could integrate with the world around them.
sentences.zh: 人们说这就像生活在黑白世界里，或者生活在一层玻璃后面，他们不再觉得能融入周围的世界。

sentences.en: Now it's been almost a year and I'm still getting Google alerts about anosmia every day.
sentences.zh: 现在已经过去快一年了，我每天仍然会收到关于嗅觉缺失症的谷歌提醒。

sentences.en: I remember talking to one scientist early in the pandemic, and she joked that if she went to a
sentences.zh: 我记得在疫情初期与一位科学家交谈时，她开玩笑说，如果她去参加

sentences.en: cocktail party and tried to describe her work, people weren't that interested or they didn't really get it.
sentences.zh: 鸡尾酒会并试图描述她的工作，人们要么不太感兴趣，要么根本听不懂。

sentences.en: And that nowadays, if she were to go to a cocktail party and explain that she was a
sentences.zh: 而现在，如果她去参加鸡尾酒会并解释说她是一位

sentences.en: smell scientist, she would be the center of attention and people would have all kinds of questions for her.
sentences.zh: 嗅觉科学家，她会成为全场的焦点，人们会问她各种各样的问题。

sentences.en: But the joke, of course, was that we don't have cocktail parties anymore.
sentences.zh: 但当然，这个笑话的前提是我们现在已经没有鸡尾酒会了。

sentences.en: So here's my story, The Forgotten Sense, read by Gabra Zachman.
sentences.zh: 这就是我的故事《被遗忘的感官》，由加布拉·扎克曼朗读。

sentences.en: Danielle Reed stopped counting after the 156th email arrived in a single afternoon.
sentences.zh: 丹妮尔·里德在收到第156封邮件后就停止了计数，而那仅仅是一个下午。

sentences.en: It was late March, and her laboratory at the Monell Chemical Senses Center in Philadelphia had abruptly gone into COVID-19 lockdown.
sentences.zh: 那是3月下旬，她位于费城莫内尔化学感官中心的实验室突然进入了新冠疫情封锁状态。

sentences.en: For weeks, there had been little to do.
sentences.zh: 几周来，几乎没什么事可做。

sentences.en: Reed, who is famous in her field for helping to discover a new family of receptors that perceive
sentences.zh: 里德在她的领域很有名，因为她帮助发现了一个感知

sentences.en: bitter flavors, had spent years studying the way human genetics affect the way we experience smell and taste.
sentences.zh: 苦味的新型受体家族，她多年来一直致力于研究人类遗传学如何影响我们对嗅觉和味觉的体验。

sentences.en: It was important but niche science that seemingly had little to do with a dangerous respiratory virus spreading around the globe.
sentences.zh: 这是一项重要但冷门的科学，似乎与在全球蔓延的危险呼吸道病毒关系不大。

sentences.en: And then one Saturday, she checked her email.
sentences.zh: 然后在一个周六，她查看了邮件。

sentences.en: Reed watched in amazement as the messages proliferated.
sentences.zh: 里德惊讶地看着邮件数量激增。

sentences.en: It wasn't how many threads there were, though that was overwhelming, but the way they seemed to grow like hydras, sprouting in all directions.
sentences.zh: 令人不知所措的不仅仅是邮件串的数量，而是它们似乎像九头蛇一样生长，向四面八方蔓延。

sentences.en: Recipients copied other people they thought might be interested in the discussion, who added more people, who added still others, across a huge range of countries and disciplines.
sentences.zh: 收件人将他们认为可能对讨论感兴趣的其他人抄送进去，这些人又添加了更多人，甚至更多人，涵盖了广泛的国家和学科。

sentences.en: The cascading emails were all responding to the same rather obscure news alert, meant for ear, nose, and throat doctors based in Britain.
sentences.zh: 这些层出不穷的邮件都在回应同一个相当晦涩的新闻提醒，该提醒原本是发给英国耳鼻喉科医生的。

sentences.en: It was titled Loss of Smell as Marker of COVID-19 Infection.
sentences.zh: 标题是《嗅觉丧失作为新冠病毒感染的标志》。

sentences.en: The week before, Claire Hopkins, the president of the British
sentences.zh: 前一周，英国

sentences.en: Rhinological Society and an author of the alert, was seeing patients in her clinic in London when she noticed something odd.
sentences.zh: 鼻科学会主席、该提醒的作者克莱尔·霍普金斯在伦敦的诊所看病时，注意到了一些奇怪的事情。

sentences.en: Hopkins, who specializes in nose and sinus diseases, especially nasal polyps, was accustomed to seeing the occasional patient, usually about one per month, whose sense of
sentences.zh: 霍普金斯专门研究鼻腔和鼻窦疾病，尤其是鼻息肉，她习惯于偶尔见到患者（通常每月约一名），他们的

sentences.en: smell disappeared after a viral infection.
sentences.zh: 嗅觉在病毒感染后消失。

sentences.en: Most of the time, such losses were fairly self-explanatory.
sentences.zh: 大多数情况下，这种丧失很容易解释。

sentences.en: A stuffy, inflamed nose keeps odorants from reaching the smell receptors at the top of the airway.
sentences.zh: 鼻塞和炎症阻碍了气味分子到达气道顶部的嗅觉受体。

sentences.en: Sometimes these receptors are also damaged by inflammation and need time to recover.
sentences.zh: 有时这些受体也会因炎症受损，需要时间恢复。

sentences.en: But patients were now arriving with no blockage or swelling, no trouble breathing, no notable symptoms, other than the sudden and mysterious disappearance of their ability to
sentences.zh: 但现在的患者到来时没有任何阻塞或肿胀，没有呼吸困难，也没有明显的症状，除了突然且神秘地丧失了

sentences.en: smell.
sentences.zh: 嗅觉。

sentences.en: And there were nine of them.
sentences.zh: 而且一下子来了九个。

sentences.en: At first, it didn't occur to Hopkins to think about the recently declared pandemic that was dominating the news.
sentences.zh: 起初，霍普金斯并没有想到最近宣布的、占据了新闻头条的全球大流行。

sentences.en: None of the patients had traveled to Italy or
sentences.zh: 这些患者中没有人去过意大利或

sentences.en: China, so they didn't meet the government's criteria for testing or quarantine.
sentences.zh: 中国，因此他们不符合政府的检测或隔离标准。

sentences.en: The virus, she understood, was not yet spreading in Britain.
sentences.zh: 她当时认为，病毒尚未在英国传播。

sentences.en: As each new patient told a strange yet similar story, she began to wonder.
sentences.zh: 随着每一位新患者讲述着奇怪而相似的故事，她开始怀疑起来。

sentences.en: A colleague in Italy, where the virus was known to be spreading, had mentioned that frontline doctors were losing their senses of smell and taste.
sentences.zh: 一位在意大利（已知病毒正在那里传播）的同事曾提到，一线医生正在失去嗅觉和味觉。

sentences.en: Hopkins assumed that a mild version of COVID-19 was causing a standard post-viral loss of smell.
sentences.zh: 霍普金斯推测，是轻微的新冠病毒感染导致了标准的病毒感染后嗅觉丧失。

sentences.en: But shortly after seeing the nine patients, she attended an online chat for physicians hosted by the
sentences.zh: 但在见到这九名患者后不久，她参加了一个由

sentences.en: American Rhinologic Society.
sentences.zh: 美国鼻科学会主办的医生在线聊天。

sentences.en: A French doctor posted that he had recently seen an increase in cases of sudden smell loss without any blockage.
sentences.zh: 一位法国医生发帖称，他最近发现突然嗅觉丧失且无任何阻塞的病例有所增加。

sentences.en: Had anyone else noticed something similar?
sentences.zh: 还有人注意到类似的情况吗？

sentences.en: Yes, several doctors from the U.S.
sentences.zh: 是的，几位来自美国的医生

sentences.en: replied.
sentences.zh: 回复了。

sentences.en: They had started to hear rumors from colleagues in Iran and Italy of odd spikes in patients who had unaccountably lost their sense of smell.
sentences.zh: 他们开始从伊朗和意大利的同事那里听到传闻，称出现了一些无法解释的嗅觉丧失患者激增的奇怪现象。

sentences.en: Hopkins decided to keep digging.
sentences.zh: 霍普金斯决定继续深挖。

sentences.en: She found that in China, an unusual number of ear, nose, and throat
sentences.zh: 她发现，在中国，有异常多的耳鼻喉

sentences.en: specialists—doctors who would have been sought out by patients troubled by an unexplained loss of smell—had contracted the virus.
sentences.zh: 专家——那些会被因不明原因嗅觉丧失而困扰的患者寻求帮助的医生——感染了该病毒。

sentences.en: A report in South Korea found that of 2,000 people with mild cases of COVID-19,
sentences.zh: 韩国的一份报告发现，在2000名新冠轻症患者中，

sentences.en: 30 percent lost their sense of smell.
sentences.zh: 30%的人失去了嗅觉。

sentences.en: The same week that patients were streaming through Hopkins' office, there was an article in a German newspaper about a virologist named Hendrik Striek,
sentences.zh: 就在患者涌入霍普金斯诊室的那一周，德国一家报纸刊登了一篇关于病毒学家亨德里克·斯特雷克的文章，

sentences.en: who went door-to-door interviewing some of the country's earliest patients.
sentences.zh: 他挨家挨户采访了该国最早的一些患者。

sentences.en: He found smell loss in two-thirds.
sentences.zh: 他发现三分之二的人出现了嗅觉丧失。

sentences.en: None of these anecdotes amounted to the sort of rigorous proof that Hopkins, with her research background, was used to seeking.
sentences.zh: 这些轶事都无法构成霍普金斯凭借其研究背景所习惯寻求的那种严谨证据。

sentences.en: She also doubted that her theory would attract much public interest, even in the face of a world-changing pandemic.
sentences.zh: 她也怀疑她的理论能否引起公众的太多兴趣，即使是在面对一场改变世界的全球大流行时。

sentences.en: A career studying smell had taught her that most people simply don't consider the sense to be particularly interesting or important.
sentences.zh: 研究嗅觉的职业生涯让她明白，大多数人根本不认为这种感官特别有趣或重要。

sentences.en: It was always hard to get financing to study smell or smell disorders, and patients who lost their olfaction often told
sentences.zh: 研究嗅觉或嗅觉障碍一直很难获得资金，而失去嗅觉的患者经常告诉

sentences.en: her that their friends and family shrugged the condition away.
sentences.zh: 她，他们的朋友和家人对这种状况不屑一顾。

sentences.en: It was only smell, after all.
sentences.zh: 毕竟，那只是嗅觉而已。

sentences.en: Still, Hopkins and Nirmal Kumar, the president of ENT UK, decided to put out an alert, hoping it would at least encourage their fellow nose doctors to take extra precautions.
sentences.zh: 尽管如此，霍普金斯和英国耳鼻喉科协会主席尼尔马尔·库马尔还是决定发布一份提醒，希望至少能鼓励他们的同行鼻科医生采取额外的预防措施。

sentences.en: Then that same weekend,
sentences.zh: 然后就在那个周末，

sentences.en: Rudy Gobert, the Utah Jazz star whose COVID-19 diagnosis caused the NBA to abruptly suspend its season
sentences.zh: 犹他爵士队的球星鲁迪·戈贝尔，其新冠病毒检测呈阳性导致 NBA 突然暂停赛季，

sentences.en: just after Gobert mocked the danger by touching all the microphones at a news conference, announced that he had lost his sense of smell.
sentences.zh: 就在戈贝尔在新闻发布会上触摸所有麦克风以嘲弄危险之后，他宣布自己失去了嗅觉。

sentences.en: Hopkins' alert ricocheted around the world, picked up by news outlets and shared on social media by people desperate for information about
sentences.zh: 霍普金斯的提醒在世界各地引起了反响，被新闻媒体报道，并在社交媒体上被那些急于了解

sentences.en: the workings of the new virus and any signs that they might already have been exposed.
sentences.zh: 这种新病毒的运作方式以及任何可能已经接触过病毒迹象的人所分享。

sentences.en: It also kept landing, over and over, in the inboxes of Danielle Reed and hundreds of other scientists who studied smell in some way.
sentences.zh: 它也一次又一次地出现在丹妮尔·里德以及数百名以某种方式研究嗅觉的科学家的收件箱中。

sentences.en: The breadth of their backgrounds was stunning, even to one another.
sentences.zh: 他们的背景之广泛令人震惊，即使是对彼此而言也是如此。

sentences.en: There were neurobiologists and otorhinolaryngologists, virologists and food scientists.
sentences.zh: 有神经生物学家和耳鼻喉科医生，有病毒学家和食品科学家。

sentences.en: There were chemists and data specialists, cognitive scientists and nutritionists, geneticists, psychologists, philosophers, an indication of how complicated the interplay of smell,
sentences.zh: 还有化学家和数据专家、认知科学家和营养学家、遗传学家、心理学家、哲学家，这表明嗅觉、

sentences.en: taste, and human life is.
sentences.zh: 味觉和人类生活之间的相互作用是多么复杂。

sentences.en: Like Hopkins, many of them were used to their work being as underappreciated as the senses they studied.
sentences.zh: 像霍普金斯一样，他们中的许多人习惯于自己的工作像他们研究的感官一样被低估。

sentences.en: Smell is a startling superpower.
sentences.zh: 嗅觉是一种惊人的超能力。

sentences.en: You can walk through someone's front door and instantly know that she recently made popcorn, drive down the street, and somehow sense that the neighbors are barbecuing.
sentences.zh: 你可以走进某人的前门，立刻知道她最近做了爆米花；开车经过街道，不知何故能感觉到邻居们正在烧烤。

sentences.en: Intuit, just as a side effect of breathing a bit of air, that this sweater has been worn, but that one hasn't.
sentences.zh: 仅仅作为呼吸空气的副作用，就能直觉地知道这件毛衣穿过，而那件没穿过。

sentences.en: That it's going to start raining soon.
sentences.zh: 知道很快就要下雨了。

sentences.en: That the grass was trimmed a few hours back.
sentences.zh: 知道草坪是几个小时前修剪的。

sentences.en: If you weren't used to it, it would seem like witchcraft.
sentences.zh: 如果你不习惯它，这看起来就像巫术。

sentences.en: But of course you are used to it.
sentences.zh: 但当然，你已经习惯了。

sentences.en: You may even take it for granted.
sentences.zh: 你甚至可能认为这是理所当然的。

sentences.en: Perhaps you would rank smell, as most adults in a
sentences.zh: 也许你会像2019年一项调查中的大多数成年人一样，将嗅觉排在

sentences.en: 2019 survey did, as the least important sense, the one you would be most willing to lose.
sentences.zh: 最不重要的感官之列，认为它是你最愿意失去的一种。

sentences.en: Perhaps you would even agree with the majority of young people who, in 2011, told McCann World Group, a marketing
sentences.zh: 也许你甚至会同意2011年麦肯世界集团（一家营销公司）调查中大多数年轻人的观点，

sentences.en: company that smell was less valuable to them than their technological devices.
sentences.zh: 他们认为嗅觉对他们来说不如科技设备有价值。

sentences.en: As PC magazine trumpeted, with a mixture of scorn and glee, majority of kids would rather lose their sense of smell than lose
sentences.zh: 正如《PC》杂志带着嘲讽和幸灾乐祸所宣扬的那样，大多数孩子宁愿失去嗅觉也不愿失去

sentences.en: Facebook.
sentences.zh: Facebook。

sentences.en: The writers of that headline seemed to see disregard for smell as shocking, a marker of a technology-obsessed and perhaps uniquely shallow generation.
sentences.zh: 该标题的作者似乎认为对嗅觉的漠视令人震惊，是一个痴迷于技术、或许极其肤浅的一代的标志。

sentences.en: That reaction would have come as a surprise to Immanuel Kant, who wrote in 1798, that smell is both the most ungrateful and the most dispensable of the senses.
sentences.zh: 这种反应会让伊曼努尔·康德感到惊讶，他在1798年写道，嗅觉是所有感官中最忘恩负义且最可有可无的。

sentences.en: Charles Darwin considered smell to be of extremely slight service to humans.
sentences.zh: 查尔斯·达尔文认为嗅觉对人类的用处极小。

sentences.en: Until quite recently, one smell researcher told me, most general medical textbooks didn't bother to include a chapter
sentences.zh: 直到最近，一位嗅觉研究人员告诉我，大多数普通医学教科书都没有费心去包含关于

sentences.en: on smell or taste, apparently considering them insignificant afterthoughts to the functioning of the human body.
sentences.zh: 嗅觉或味觉的章节，显然认为它们在人体功能中是微不足道的附带事项。

sentences.en: From Plato and Aristotle—Plato considered smells half-formed, and Aristotle wrote
sentences.zh: 从柏拉图和亚里士多德——柏拉图认为气味是未成形的，而亚里士多德写道

sentences.en: that man smells poorly—to Descartes and Hegel, one called vision the noblest of the senses, while the
sentences.zh: 人类嗅觉很差——到笛卡尔和黑格尔，前者称视觉是最高贵的感官，而

sentences.en: other dismissed smell and taste as too pedestrian and vulgar to be included among the senses in his aesthetics.
sentences.zh: 后者则在美学中将嗅觉和味觉斥为过于平庸和粗俗，不配列入感官之中。

sentences.en: We have spent centuries writing off our own sense of smell.
sentences.zh: 几个世纪以来，我们一直在否定自己的嗅觉。

sentences.en: One reason we have discounted smelling is our belief that we're bad at it.
sentences.zh: 我们轻视嗅觉的一个原因是，我们相信自己在这方面很差劲。

sentences.en: Smell was the province of lesser animals, we told ourselves, of pigs rooting out truffles and sharks scenting blood, while humans were creatures of reason
sentences.zh: 我们告诉自己，嗅觉是低等动物的领域，是猪寻找松露和鲨鱼嗅出血液的本能，而人类是理性的生物

sentences.en: and intellect, who managed to stand up and grow huge brains and leave that life far behind and literally below us.
sentences.zh: 和智力生物，我们成功地站立起来，长出了巨大的大脑，并将那种生活远远抛在身后，甚至在字面意义上踩在脚下。

sentences.en: Scientists followed Paul Broca, a 19th-century neuroscientist, in pointing to the relative
sentences.zh: 科学家们追随19世纪神经科学家保罗·布罗卡的观点，指出我们嗅球的相对

sentences.en: smallness of our olfactory bulbs as evidence that our brains had triumphed over them, and likewise over the need to pay much attention to smell at all.
sentences.zh: 微小，作为我们大脑战胜了它们、从而也战胜了对嗅觉给予太多关注的必要性的证据。

sentences.en: In the late 1950s, a pioneering ear, nose, and throat specialist,
sentences.zh: 20世纪50年代末，一位开创性的耳鼻喉科专家，

sentences.en: Victor Negus, summed up the consensus view in a book about the comparative anatomy of the nose.
sentences.zh: 维克多·内格斯，在一本关于鼻子比较解剖学的书中总结了共识观点。

sentences.en: The human mind is an inadequate agent with which to study olfaction, the specialist wrote, for the
sentences.zh: 这位专家写道，人类的心智是一个不足以研究嗅觉的媒介，因为

sentences.en: reason that in man the sense of smell is relatively feeble and not of great significance.
sentences.zh: 在人类身上，嗅觉相对微弱，意义不大。

sentences.en: For centuries, when scientists studied smell at all, they tended to focus on isolating particular odorants, they thought
sentences.zh: 几个世纪以来，当科学家们研究嗅觉时，他们倾向于专注于分离特定的气味分子，他们认为

sentences.en: they could find the odor version of primary colors, and creating elaborate organizational systems that shuffled them into various categories.
sentences.zh: 他们可以找到原色的气味版本，并创建复杂的组织系统，将它们归入各种类别。

sentences.en: History is littered with the wrecks of universal classifications of smell, the smell scientist Avery Gilbert wrote in her book What the Nose Knows.
sentences.zh: 嗅觉科学家艾弗里·吉尔伯特在她的书《鼻子知道什么》中写道，历史上充斥着通用气味分类法的残骸。

sentences.en: Questions of how humans smell, and how our smelling in turn interacts with our bodies, our health, and our behavior,
sentences.zh: 关于人类如何嗅闻，以及我们的嗅觉如何反过来与我们的身体、健康和行为相互作用的问题，

sentences.en: were of far less intereSt. The sense, after all, was seen as practically vestigial, an often handy,
sentences.zh: 受到的关注要少得多。毕竟，这种感官被视为几乎是退化的，是一种通常方便、

sentences.en: sometimes pleasant, but ultimately unimportant holdover from our distant paSt. The notion of smell as vestigial has itself come to seem outmoded.
sentences.zh: 有时令人愉悦，但最终并不重要的遥远过去的遗留物。将嗅觉视为退化器官的观念本身已经显得过时了。

sentences.en: That's because of a renaissance in smell science.
sentences.zh: 这是因为嗅觉科学的复兴。

sentences.en: While we have long understood the basic mechanisms of vision and audition, it has been less than 30
sentences.zh: 虽然我们长期以来一直了解视觉和听觉的基本机制，但距离我们识别出那些让我们感知并理解周围气味的神经受体，

sentences.en: years since the neural receptors that allow us to perceive and make sense of the smells around us were even identified.
sentences.zh: 甚至还不到30年。

sentences.en: The discoverers, Linda Buck and Richard Axel, were awarded the Nobel Prize in 2004.
sentences.zh: 发现者琳达·巴克（Linda Buck）和理查德·阿克塞尔（Richard Axel）于2004年被授予诺贝尔奖。

sentences.en: The revelation opened the door to a new way of understanding the olfactory system, as well as to a new, ever-expanding world of research.
sentences.zh: 这一发现开启了理解嗅觉系统的新方式，也打开了一个全新的、不断扩展的研究领域。

sentences.en: A system assumed to be unsophisticated and insignificant turned out to be quite the opposite.
sentences.zh: 一个曾被认为简单且无关紧要的系统，结果却恰恰相反。

sentences.en: Where vision depends on four kinds of receptors, rods, and three types of cones.
sentences.zh: 视觉依赖于四种受体：视杆细胞和三种视锥细胞。

sentences.en: Smell uses about 400 receptors, which are together estimated to be able to detect as many as a trillion smells.
sentences.zh: 嗅觉使用了大约400种受体，据估计它们总共能探测多达一万亿种气味。

sentences.en: The complexity of the system is such that we're still unable to predict how, or even if, a given chemical will be perceived by our olfactory system.
sentences.zh: 该系统的复杂程度之高，以至于我们至今仍无法预测某种特定的化学物质是否会被我们的嗅觉系统感知，或者将如何被感知。

sentences.en: The old quest to map odorants and their perception is now understood to be a wildly complicated undertaking.
sentences.zh: 长期以来绘制气味及其感知图谱的探索，现在被认为是一项极其复杂的工程。

sentences.en: Joel Mainland, a neuroscientist at the Monell Center who is working on the problem, told me that while maps of color vision are easily presented in two dimensions,
sentences.zh: 莫内尔中心（Monell Center）的神经科学家乔尔·梅恩兰（Joel Mainland）正在研究这个问题，他告诉我，虽然色觉图谱很容易在二维平面上呈现，

sentences.en: an eventual olfactory map might require many more.
sentences.zh: 但最终的嗅觉图谱可能需要更多的维度。

sentences.en: Recent studies have begun to puncture our conviction that we are too sophisticated to be good at smelling.
sentences.zh: 近期的研究开始打破我们那种“人类太高级，所以嗅觉不灵敏”的固有观念。

sentences.en: Our brains know the difference between exercise sweat and fear sweat, and between a glass of wine that has recently contained a fruit fly, and one that has not.
sentences.zh: 我们的大脑能够区分运动后的汗味和恐惧时的汗味，也能分辨出一杯刚掉进果蝇的葡萄酒和一杯没有果蝇的葡萄酒。

sentences.en: They seem to compel us to sniff our fingers shortly after we shake other people's hands, searching for information about them that we're not consciously aware of processing.
sentences.zh: 当我们与他人握手后，似乎会不由自主地嗅闻自己的手指，寻找那些我们并未意识到正在处理的关于对方的信息。

sentences.en: One inventive study found that, provided we're willing to crawl around with our faces in the grass,
sentences.zh: 一项富有创意的研究发现，只要我们愿意趴在草地上，

sentences.en: humans are fully capable of finding a scent trail while blindfolded, not as well as a dog, granted, but we can follow it.
sentences.zh: 人类完全有能力在蒙住眼睛的情况下追踪气味，虽然不如狗，但我们确实可以做到。

sentences.en: Another found that we can tell, just from sniffing a t-shirt another person has worn, whether that person's immune system is similar to our own.
sentences.zh: 另一项研究发现，仅凭嗅闻别人穿过的T恤，我们就能判断对方的免疫系统是否与我们相似。

sentences.en: If it's different, we find the person more attractive.
sentences.zh: 如果不同，我们会觉得对方更有吸引力。

sentences.en: But here's what's really impressive.
sentences.zh: 但真正令人印象深刻的是这一点。

sentences.en: Our noses can also distinguish between two groups of mice that have different immune systeMs. Several years ago, the Rutgers scientist John McGann took a
sentences.zh: 我们的鼻子甚至能区分两组免疫系统不同的小鼠。几年前，罗格斯大学（Rutgers）的科学家约翰·麦甘（John McGann）对

sentences.en: critical look at Broca's 150-year-old dismissal of our olfactory bulbs and found it to be mistaken.
sentences.zh: 布罗卡（Broca）150年前对人类嗅球的否定观点进行了批判性审视，发现那是错误的。

sentences.en: Our bulbs are shaped a little differently, but when you compare how many neurons they hold with those of other mammals, humans are solidly in the middle of the pack.
sentences.zh: 我们的嗅球形状略有不同，但当你将其神经元数量与其他哺乳动物进行比较时，人类处于中等水平。

sentences.en: There are, he pointed out, even some odors we can smell better than rodents or canines can.
sentences.zh: 他指出，甚至有些气味我们比啮齿动物或犬类闻得更灵敏。

sentences.en: A much-discussed unit of measurement in smell studies is the JND, the just noticeable difference, or the degree to which chemicals have to differ from one
sentences.zh: 嗅觉研究中一个常被讨论的测量单位是JND，即“最小可觉差”，也就是化学物质必须达到多大程度的差异，

sentences.en: another in order for us to tell them apart.
sentences.zh: 我们才能分辨出它们的不同。

sentences.en: In November, a new paper in Nature advanced the quest for a map of olfactory perception by creating a model that can predict what odorants will smell like by contrasting
sentences.zh: 11月，《自然》（Nature）杂志发表的一篇新论文通过创建一个模型，对比化学物质与其他气味的成分，从而预测气味闻起来是什么样，这推进了对嗅觉感知图谱的探索。

sentences.en: their chemical makeup with that of other smells.
sentences.zh: 其化学构成与其它气味进行对比。

sentences.en: The work relied on volunteers comparing hundreds of different odors and found them to be almost frustratingly good at it.
sentences.zh: 这项工作依赖于志愿者对数百种不同气味的比较，结果发现他们在这方面表现得好到令人沮丧。

sentences.en: The failure to reach an absolute JND provides for yet additional evidence of an exquisite sense of smell in humans, the author said.
sentences.zh: 作者表示，未能达到绝对的JND，反而为人类拥有敏锐的嗅觉提供了进一步的证据。

sentences.en: To rephrase this result, it is simply very hard to generate two multi-component odorants that humans cannot discriminate.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，要制造出两种人类无法区分的多组分气味，实在是非常困难。

sentences.en: One of the authors, Noam Sobol of the Weitzman Institute of Science in Israel, also worked
sentences.zh: 其中一位作者，以色列魏茨曼科学研究所（Weitzman Institute of Science）的诺姆·索博尔（Noam Sobol），也参与了

sentences.en: on the scent trail study and the one about handshakes, as well as a study that found that an automatic sniff
sentences.zh: 气味追踪研究和握手研究，以及一项发现自动嗅闻反应的研究——

sentences.en: reaction – taking longer breaths when something smells good and shorter ones when something smells bad – is a reliable predictor that someone will eventually wake up from a coma.
sentences.zh: 即闻到好闻的东西时呼吸变长，闻到难闻的东西时呼吸变短——这是预测昏迷病人是否会苏醒的可靠指标。

sentences.en: In the early days of the pandemic, he was spending his days at testing centers in Tel Aviv, trying to figure out whether an artificial nose could sniff out the novel coronavirus.
sentences.zh: 在疫情初期，他每天都在特拉维夫的检测中心工作，试图弄清楚人造鼻子是否能嗅出新型冠状病毒。

sentences.en: Not a crazy notion, because dogs are learning to do it, and because at least one human has proved her ability to identify sufferers of
sentences.zh: 这并非疯狂的想法，因为狗正在学习这样做，而且至少已经有一名人类证明了她有能力仅凭嗅觉识别出

sentences.en: Parkinson's disease just by smelling them.
sentences.zh: 帕金森病患者。

sentences.en: Sobol and his colleagues also started a website,
sentences.zh: 索博尔和他的同事还创办了一个网站，

sentences.en: SmellTracker.org, where people who were worried about COVID could track changes in their ability to
sentences.zh: SmellTracker.org，让担心感染新冠的人们可以追踪自己识别

sentences.en: smell a variety of common household iteMs. We think that smell is less important to us than our other senses only because we're fooling ourselves, Sobol told me.
sentences.zh: 各种常见家居用品气味的能力的变化。索博尔告诉我，我们认为嗅觉不如其他感官重要，只是因为我们在自欺欺人。

sentences.en: After all, you wouldn't eat a beautiful cake if it smelled like sewage, but you would probably try some ugly gloop that smelled like cinnamon.
sentences.zh: 毕竟，如果一块漂亮的蛋糕闻起来像污水，你肯定不会吃；但如果一块难看的糊状物闻起来像肉桂，你很可能会尝尝。

sentences.en: COVID, he hypothesized, could kick off a sort of global reckoning, forcing our conscious minds to recognize what our brains have known all along.
sentences.zh: 他推测，新冠疫情可能会引发一场全球性的反思，迫使我们的意识去承认大脑一直以来所知道的事实。

sentences.en: People are unaware smell is important until they lose it, he said.
sentences.zh: 他说，人们在失去嗅觉之前，根本意识不到它的重要性。

sentences.en: And then they're terrified.
sentences.zh: 而一旦失去，他们就会感到恐惧。

sentences.en: The growing mess of emails that followed Hopkins's alert in March quickly became so unwieldy that the scientists decided to move to a more formalized group.
sentences.zh: 霍普金斯（Hopkins）在3月份发出警报后，随之而来的电子邮件变得越来越多，以至于科学家们决定成立一个更正式的组织。

sentences.en: Within days, it had 500 members from dozens of countries and a name, the Global Consortium for
sentences.zh: 几天之内，它就拥有了来自几十个国家的500名成员，并取名为“全球化学感官研究联盟”（Global Consortium for Chemosensory Research）。

sentences.en: Chemosensory Research.
sentences.zh: 化学感官研究联盟。

sentences.en: The group eventually stabilized at around 630 members from 64 countries.
sentences.zh: 该组织最终稳定在大约630名成员，来自64个国家。

sentences.en: We decided to become a global organization, explained Valentina Parma, a psychologist who, along with Reed and seven others, helped found the GCCR's leadership committee.
sentences.zh: 心理学家瓦伦蒂娜·帕尔马（Valentina Parma）解释说：“我们决定成为一个全球性组织。”她与里德（Reed）及其他七人共同帮助建立了GCCR的领导委员会。

sentences.en: We all got together to try to figure out what's going on.
sentences.zh: 我们聚在一起，试图弄清楚到底发生了什么。

sentences.en: The sheer number of questions was daunting.
sentences.zh: 问题的数量之多令人望而生畏。

sentences.en: How many COVID patients experienced smell loss?
sentences.zh: 有多少新冠患者经历了嗅觉丧失？

sentences.en: How fully did smell disappear?
sentences.zh: 嗅觉丧失的程度有多严重？

sentences.en: Smell loss is known as anosmia when it's complete and hyposmia when it's partial.
sentences.zh: 嗅觉完全丧失被称为嗅觉缺失症（anosmia），部分丧失则被称为嗅觉减退症（hyposmia）。

sentences.en: Was COVID-related smell loss truly distinct from that caused by other viruses?
sentences.zh: 新冠相关的嗅觉丧失是否真的与其他病毒引起的有所不同？

sentences.en: How many patients would be able to recover their olfaction?
sentences.zh: 有多少患者能够恢复嗅觉？

sentences.en: And how long might it take?
sentences.zh: 需要多长时间？

sentences.en: Many patients were reporting loss of taste as well as smell, but this too was complicated.
sentences.zh: 许多患者报告说不仅失去了嗅觉，还失去了味觉，但这也很复杂。

sentences.en: Thanks to a process called oral referral, which causes us to perceive what's happening in the nose as if it's inside the mouth, smell is integral to our experience of taste.
sentences.zh: 多亏了一种叫做“口腔转导”的过程，它让我们把鼻子里发生的感觉感知为在口腔内发生，嗅觉是我们味觉体验中不可或缺的一部分。

sentences.en: People often struggle to separate the two, certain that they have lost their sense of taste when the taste buds, which detect only
sentences.zh: 人们往往难以区分两者，确信自己失去了味觉，而实际上，只能检测

sentences.en: sweet, salty, bitter, sour, and umami flavors, remain fully functional.
sentences.zh: 甜、咸、苦、酸和鲜味的味蕾功能依然完好。

sentences.en: There was also the question of the sensations we experience through neither olfaction nor taste, but via the nerves of our trigeminal system.
sentences.zh: 还有一个问题是，我们通过三叉神经系统感受到的感觉，既不是嗅觉也不是味觉。

sentences.en: The coolness of mint, the spice of peppers, the bubble of carbonation.
sentences.zh: 薄荷的清凉、辣椒的辛辣、碳酸饮料的气泡感。

sentences.en: Were these also affected?
sentences.zh: 这些是否也受到了影响？

sentences.en: The three, together, are known as our chemosensory senses, those we use to detect the presence of chemicals in our environment.
sentences.zh: 这三者合称为我们的化学感官，是我们用来探测环境中化学物质存在的感官。

sentences.en: Answering these questions could help solve the most urgent puzzle.
sentences.zh: 回答这些问题有助于解开最紧迫的谜题。

sentences.en: What exactly was happening inside patients to make their sense of smell disappear in such an unusual way?
sentences.zh: 患者体内到底发生了什么，导致他们的嗅觉以这种不同寻常的方式消失？

sentences.en: Could COVID-related smell loss teach us anything new about how the virus worked?
sentences.zh: 新冠相关的嗅觉丧失能让我们对病毒的工作机制有新的了解吗？

sentences.en: Or about how we did?
sentences.zh: 或者对我们自身有新的认识？

sentences.en: As a panicked world closed down around them, members of the GCCR started meeting online every day, working on a plan to survey people with respiratory illnesses about their
sentences.zh: 当恐慌的世界在他们周围封闭时，GCCR的成员开始每天在线开会，制定计划调查呼吸道疾病患者的

sentences.en: symptoMs. There were so many eager researchers, from so many countries, that the survey was quickly translated into more than 30 languages.
sentences.zh: 症状。来自许多国家的科研人员热情高涨，调查问卷很快被翻译成30多种语言。

sentences.en: Though the group considered using several of the more objective olfaction tests developed in recent decades, they decided, given the urgency of the

sentences.en: They quickly established that people who lost smell and tested positive for the coronavirus weren't encountering the typical nasal blockage.

sentences.en: They often referred to the loss as sudden and creepy.

sentences.en: And that they were also noticing genuine impairments not just to their olfaction, but in many cases to their taste and trigeminal sensations as well.
sentences.zh: 而且他们还注意到，不仅嗅觉受到了真正的损害，在许多情况下，味觉和三叉神经感觉也受到了影响。

sentences.en: This clearly wasn't the typical pathology of smell loss following a virus.

sentences.en: The scientists also noticed that a disconnect was forming between what the data showed and how the wider world responded.
sentences.zh: 科学家们还注意到，数据所显示的与外界的反应之间正在形成一种脱节。

sentences.en: Early on, data from apps for tracking symptoms showed that smell loss was more common than the fever or cough the virus was known for.
sentences.zh: 早期，症状追踪应用程序的数据显示，嗅觉丧失比该病毒众所周知的发烧或咳嗽更为常见。

sentences.en: It also had the diagnostic advantage of pointing directly to COVID rather than to another respiratory illness.
sentences.zh: 它还具有诊断优势，即直接指向新冠，而不是其他呼吸道疾病。

sentences.en: And yet, schools and restaurants and airports continued to use forehead thermometers to screen for fevers, a symptom that many people with COVID never experienced.
sentences.zh: 然而，学校、餐馆和机场继续使用额温枪来筛查发烧，而许多新冠患者从未出现过发烧症状。

sentences.zh: 后来，GCCR的分析显示，嗅觉丧失实际上是新冠最可靠的预测指标，即使对于那些评估自己嗅觉丧失情况的人来说也是如此，而

sentences.zh: 里德和其他研究人员还发现，客观的嗅觉测试（患者必须通过实际刺激来证明自己）能够

sentences.en: to catch many extra COVID cases among people who failed to realize when their sense of smell had changed.
sentences.zh: 在那些没有意识到自己嗅觉发生变化的人群中，捕捉到许多额外的新冠病例。

sentences.en: The better we ask questions about smell, Parma says, the more people we find.
sentences.zh: 帕尔马说，我们关于嗅觉的问题问得越好，发现的病例就越多。

sentences.en: In Britain, Hopkins was growing frustrated.
sentences.zh: 在英国，霍普金斯感到越来越沮丧。

sentences.zh: 几周过去了，嗅觉丧失仍然没有出现在国家医疗服务体系（NHS）认可的官方

sentences.en: symptoms recognized by the National Health Service, a list that determined who qualified or didn't for coronavirus testing.
sentences.zh: 症状列表中，而该列表决定了谁有资格进行新冠检测。

sentences.en: One of her patients, a physiotherapist, was told to keep reporting to the ICU where he worked, even though his family was sick and he had lost his sense of smell.
sentences.zh: 她的一位患者，一名物理治疗师，被告知要继续去他工作的重症监护室上班，尽管他的家人病了，而且他自己也失去了嗅觉。

sentences.en: He convinced his team that he should be allowed to self-isolate, but Hopkins wondered how many other people were in similar situations, sent out

sentences.zh: 轻症患者中表现明显的症状。

sentences.en: people with only mild disease.
sentences.zh: 但她也认为，还有一个与病毒无关的重要因素。

sentences.en: But she also believed that there was another important factor unrelated to the virus.
sentences.zh: 新冠疫情降临在一个长期以来一直不重视嗅觉的世界里。

sentences.en: COVID arrived in a world that had spent far too long not taking smell seriously.
sentences.zh: 这或许是一个迟来的披露时刻。

sentences.en: This may be the moment for a belated disclosure.
sentences.zh: 关于嗅觉科学，我感兴趣的部分原因是我自己就是嗅觉缺失者。

sentences.en: Part of what interests me about the science of smell is that I myself am anosmic.
sentences.zh: 对于嗅觉看起来像超能力的外行来说？

sentences.zh: 那个人就是我。

sentences.zh: 我不知道我的嗅觉缺失是先天的，还是我的嗅觉在我有记忆之前就停止了工作。

sentences.zh: 我小时候确实得过很多次耳部感染，众所周知这会损害嗅觉。

sentences.zh: 而且嗅觉缺失者通常要到十几岁时，才完全意识到自己与众不同。

sentences.en: and it's common for anosmic people not to realize fully that they're different until, on average, they're early teens.
sentences.zh: 我当时大概就是那个年纪，姐姐回家发现我正幸福地抱着被臭鼬喷过的狗，事情的真相才开始浮出水面。

sentences.en: That's about how old I was when my sister came home to find me blissfully cuddling our skunk-sprayed dog, and the pieces began to fall into place.
sentences.zh: 多年后，还是这位姐姐及时赶回家，阻止了我在一个不小心充满了丙烷的小屋里点火柴。

sentences.zh: 在了解什么是嗅觉缺失症之前，每当人们提起他们闻到的东西时，我总以为这是一种我还没学会的技能，是我自己没做对。

sentences.zh: 当你失去嗅觉时，你会注意到的一件事是，有嗅觉的人花在谈论它上面的时间是多么多。

sentences.en: they were smelling, that this was a skill I had yet to figure out, that I just wasn't doing it right.
sentences.zh: 朋友们总是好奇我是否能尝出食物的味道。

sentences.zh: 我热爱食物，尽管我主要关心的是质地和味蕾感知到的味道。

sentences.en: Friends are always curious about whether I can taste food.
sentences.zh: 但那是他们想象中的主要区别。

sentences.en: I love food, though I care primarily about textures and the flavors the actual taste buds perceive.
sentences.zh: 他们似乎没有意识到嗅觉在他们脑海中挥之不去的其他方式。

sentences.en: But that's the main difference they imagine.
sentences.zh: 嗅觉没什么大不了，直到它消失。

sentences.en: Then there were those who gained it back slowly, over the course of many months.
sentences.zh: 这就是另一位GCCR成员克丽丝·凯利（Chrissy Kelly）所担心的可能发生的情况。

sentences.en: But there was a smaller percentage who, at six months, didn't seem to be recovering it at all.

sentences.en: This was what Chrissy Kelly, another GCCR member, feared might happen.
sentences.zh: 接下来的两年里，她感到抑郁、健忘，感觉自己与能闻到气味时的自己完全不同。

sentences.en: In 2012, she lost her own sense of smell after fighting a virus she caught on an airplane.

sentences.zh: 本月，德克萨斯州一个家庭的成员因新冠失去了嗅觉，在唯一未受感染的家庭成员——一名青少年——闻到烟味后，他们险些从火灾中逃生

sentences.en: and woke everyone else up.
sentences.zh: 并叫醒了其他人。

sentences.en: around them.

sentences.zh: 食物闻起来像汽油或香烟，或者香味沐浴露闻起来像烧焦的橡胶。

sentences.zh: 正如帕尔马所说，对于视觉，我们在立场上达成一致。

sentences.zh: 事实证明，这非常重要。

sentences.en: That turns out to matter quite a lot.
sentences.zh: 这非常重要。

sentences.en: Being able to describe and discuss what we smell helps us smell it better.
sentences.zh: 能够描述和讨论我们闻到的东西，有助于我们更好地嗅闻它。

sentences.zh: 想想侍酒师，他们学习辨别葡萄酒中独特香气的方法，很大程度上是通过学习一套专门的语言来实现的。

sentences.zh: 这些词汇的作用方式与颜色词非常相似，每一个词都描述了气味体验中固有的某种特质，而不是将其与其他事物进行比较。

sentences.en: People who grow up in such cultures are better at detecting, discriminating, and naming odors.

sentences.en: One also doubts that they would require a scientific renaissance to tell them that smell matters.
sentences.zh: 人们也怀疑，他们是否需要一场科学复兴来告诉他们嗅觉很重要。

sentences.en: Western psychology is frequently and justifiably criticized for being skewed because such a disproportionate number of its study subjects come from just a few weird countries.
sentences.zh: 西方心理学经常且合理地受到批评，因为它存在偏差，因为其研究对象中不成比例地来自少数几个“怪异”（WEIRD）国家。

sentences.en: Western, educated, industrial, rich, and democratic.
sentences.zh: 即西方（Western）、受过教育（Educated）、工业化（Industrial）、富有（Rich）和民主（Democratic）的国家。

sentences.en: Smell scientists have also begun to talk about what it means that many early scientists and theoreticians of perception, as well as the people they studied, were also ODD.
sentences.zh: 嗅觉科学家也开始讨论这样一个事实的意义：许多早期的感知科学家和理论家，以及他们研究的对象，也都是“怪异”（ODD）的。

sentences.en: They were older people whose senses of smell were therefore naturally diminished, they lived in deodorized societies where many natural smells were unwelcome, and they were also
sentences.zh: 他们是老年人，因此嗅觉自然减退；他们生活在除臭的社会中，许多自然气味是不受欢迎的；而且他们

sentences.en: generally desensitized to smells because of living in cultures that paid little attention to them,
sentences.zh: 通常对气味不敏感，因为他们生活在几乎不关注气味的文化中，

sentences.en: and because of the dulling effects of urban pollution and even, perhaps, their common affinity for smoking.
sentences.zh: 也因为城市污染的迟钝效应，甚至可能还因为他们普遍有吸烟的习惯。

sentences.en: It may be no wonder at all that they found smell so unworthy of consideration.
sentences.zh: 难怪他们觉得嗅觉根本不值得考虑。

sentences.en: This leads to some interesting questions.
sentences.zh: 这引出了一些有趣的问题。

sentences.en: What if we've spent so much time dismissing the importance of smell because of some odd, or ODD, accident of history?
sentences.zh: 如果我们因为某种奇怪的（或“怪异的”）历史偶然，而花了这么多时间去否定嗅觉的重要性，那会怎样？

sentences.en: And what if we might rediscover it, in part, because of another?
sentences.zh: 如果我们能部分地因为另一个偶然事件而重新发现它，又会怎样？

sentences.en: As the virus ripped through New York City last spring, Pablo Meyer, another GCCR member, stayed inside his apartment, listening to ambulance sirens.
sentences.zh: 去年春天，当病毒席卷纽约市时，GCCR 的另一位成员 Pablo Meyer 待在公寓里，听着救护车的警笛声。

sentences.en: Every morning, he tested his own sense of smell to assuage the persistent fear that he, like so many of his neighbors, had contracted the coronavirus.
sentences.zh: 每天早上，他都会测试自己的嗅觉，以缓解那种挥之不去的恐惧——担心自己像许多邻居一样感染了新冠病毒。

sentences.en: He then spent his days reading replies to the GCCR survey as they poured in from around the world.
sentences.zh: 然后，他每天花时间阅读从世界各地涌入的 GCCR 调查回复。

sentences.en: One person's sense of smell disappeared entirely over the course of cooking a single meal.
sentences.zh: 有人在做一顿饭的过程中，嗅觉完全消失了。

sentences.en: Someone found a boyfriend's signature pasta dish suddenly disgusting, while someone else doused a worryingly bland breakfast with hot sauce to no effect.
sentences.zh: 有人发现男朋友的招牌意面突然变得令人作呕，而另一个人在令人担忧的平淡早餐上浇了辣酱，却毫无效果。

sentences.en: A sommelier failed to notice that the cat's litter box was full, and a self-described former bloodhound, always the
sentences.zh: 一位侍酒师没注意到猫砂盆满了，而一个自称曾经是“猎犬”的人，总是

sentences.en: first in any group of people to notice an odor, nearly gagged on food that smelled of nothing.
sentences.zh: 人群中第一个闻到气味的人，在吃闻起来什么味儿都没有的食物时，差点呕吐。

sentences.en: Nothing is savory anymore, someone wrote.
sentences.zh: 有人写道，什么东西都没有味道了。

sentences.en: Coffee is just bitter.
sentences.zh: 咖啡只有苦味。

sentences.en: A cake is just sweet.
sentences.zh: 蛋糕只有甜味。

sentences.en: A burger is just salty.
sentences.zh: 汉堡只有咸味。

sentences.en: Meyer began to feel as if he knew the people personally, the ones who described smells in terms of tea and fruit, or meat and gasoline, or blue Powerade and lollipops.
sentences.zh: Meyer 开始觉得他仿佛亲自认识这些人，那些用茶和水果，或者肉和汽油，或者蓝色佳得乐和棒棒糖来描述气味的人。

sentences.en: The way they described their senses felt so intimate, he said later, you could almost see the type of person they are.
sentences.zh: 他说，他们描述感官的方式感觉非常亲密，你几乎可以看到他们是什么样的人。

sentences.en: He was becoming convinced that people believe they are bad at describing smells simply because they so often
sentences.zh: 他开始确信，人们认为自己不擅长描述气味，仅仅是因为他们经常

sentences.en: are asked to do so in labs, sniffing single, isolated molecules, when the more familiar odor of coffee

sentences.en: is a blend of many hundreds of them, cloistered away from the context of their real lives and the smells that actually mattered to them.
sentences.zh: 是数百种分子的混合体，它们被隔离在真实生活环境之外，远离那些对他们真正重要的气味。

sentences.en: Given the right opportunity, he said, people become very, very verbal.
sentences.zh: 他说，只要给予适当的机会，人们会变得非常、非常健谈。

sentences.en: For Meyer, an IBM researcher who specializes in using algorithms to analyze biological data,

sentences.zh: 也是坚持 GCCR 调查应包含开放文本框的人之一，这是一个令人兴奋的消息。

sentences.en: For years, scientists studying smell have been working off just a few deeply deficient datasets that link different chemicals and the way humans perceive them.
sentences.zh: 多年来，研究嗅觉的科学家一直依靠少数几个深度匮乏的数据集，这些数据集将不同的化学物质与人类感知它们的方式联系起来。

sentences.en: There was, for example, a record created in the late 1960s by a single perfumer who described

sentences.zh: 数千种气味，而且一项又一项研究都依赖于 1985 年出版的一份单一气味特征图谱。

sentences.en: It drew on the observations of volunteers who had been asked to smell various single molecules

sentences.zh: 最近，Meyer 和许多其他人一直在使用一个新的数据集，这是纽约洛克菲勒大学的科学家们辛苦创建并于 2016 年发表的。

sentences.en: I visited the lab in 2014 while Leslie Vosshall and her colleagues were building their data,
sentences.zh: 2014 年我参观了该实验室，当时 Leslie Vosshall 和她的同事们正在建立他们的数据，

sentences.en: and was surprised to find I could smell one of the vials, though it probably just triggered my trigeminal system.
sentences.zh: 我很惊讶地发现我能闻到其中一个小瓶的味道，尽管那可能只是刺激了我的三叉神经系统。

sentences.en: When I told Vosshall that it seemed minty, she replied, really?
sentences.zh: 当我告诉 Vosshall 它闻起来像薄荷时，她回答说，真的吗？

sentences.en: Most people say dirty socks.
sentences.zh: 大多数人说是脏袜子。

sentences.en: But while the new dataset was a significant improvement—55 people smelled 480 different molecules, rating them by intensity, pleasantness, familiarity, and how well
sentences.zh: 但是，虽然这个新数据集有了显著改进——55 个人闻了 480 种不同的分子，根据强度、愉悦度、熟悉度以及它们与

sentences.en: They were interested in the possibilities of natural language processing, a branch of machine learning that uses algorithms to analyze the patterns of human expression.

sentences.zh: Secchi 已经在利用这项技术，通过分析人们说话方式的细节，来预测阿尔茨海默病的最早发病期，此时该病最易于治疗。

sentences.zh: 许多研究人员曾撰文探讨利用人工智能最终绘制出

sentences.zh: 但一直没有足够的数据可用。

sentences.zh: 现在，新冠疫情为研究人员提供了一个庞大而复杂的数据集，将嗅觉体验与特定疾病的进展联系起来。

sentences.zh: 它不受数值排名、单分子或少数几个提供的形容词的限制，而是允许人们自由地谈论现实世界中真实的气味，

sentences.zh: 展现它们复杂而主观的魅力。

sentences.en: After that, what will be really interesting are the applications we can't yet imagine.
sentences.zh: 在那之后，真正有趣的是我们目前还无法想象的应用。

sentences.zh: 10 月初，我在网络研讨会上看到

sentences.en: Using data from France, where an especially large number of people had filled out the survey,

sentences.en: researchers overlaid the timing and geography of self-reported smell and taste loss with lockdowns and hospital admissions.

sentences.en: They found that increases in anosmia had been a more timely indicator of surges in viral transmission than the data the government was using.
sentences.zh: 他们发现，嗅觉丧失的增加比政府使用的数据更能及时地预示病毒传播的激增。

sentences.en: They could also see the effects of lockdowns clearly in the surveys.
sentences.zh: 他们还能在调查中清楚地看到封锁措施的影响。

sentences.en: New onset smell and taste loss began to decline five days after lockdowns began, while it took 15 days for the government's hospital-based
sentences.zh: 新发嗅觉和味觉丧失在封锁开始五天后开始下降，而政府基于医院的

sentences.en: indicators to show that they were working.
sentences.zh: 指标则需要 15 天才能显示出封锁措施正在发挥作用。

sentences.en: Smell and taste tracking could be a crucial tool for detecting next waves, Paredaloth argued.
sentences.zh: Paredaloth 认为，嗅觉和味觉追踪可能是检测下一波疫情的关键工具。

sentences.en: Yet it remained difficult to get smell taken seriously.
sentences.zh: 然而，让人们认真对待嗅觉仍然很困难。

sentences.en: When someone asked how that fact was being communicated to governments, there was a lot of rueful laughter.
sentences.zh: 当有人问这一事实是如何传达给政府时，现场发出了一阵无奈的笑声。

sentences.en: Europe's autumn spike, which eventually brought new lockdowns, began shortly afterward.
sentences.zh: 欧洲的秋季疫情高峰，最终导致了新的封锁，不久之后就开始了。

sentences.en: Parma thought that the GCCR message board would start to quiet down once lockdowns ended and people went back to their own labs.
sentences.zh: Parma 原本以为，一旦封锁结束，人们回到各自的实验室，GCCR 的留言板就会安静下来。

sentences.en: But instead she saw more and more proposals for ways to study the group's data, and more small groups of new collaborators spinning off to chase new questions.
sentences.zh: 但相反，她看到了越来越多关于研究该组数据的提案，以及更多由新合作者组成的小组分化出来，去追寻新的问题。

sentences.en: Dalton imagines a future in which smell checks on infants and children, which could give far more insight into their overall health than a hearing test, become routine.
sentences.zh: Dalton 设想了一个未来，届时对婴儿和儿童进行嗅觉检查将成为常规，这比听力测试能提供更多关于他们整体健康的见解。

sentences.en: She and Reed, as well as some other researchers, have begun developing coronavirus screening tests for public places based not on fevers, but on ability to smell.
sentences.zh: 她和 Reed 以及其他一些研究人员已经开始开发用于公共场所的新冠病毒筛查测试，不是基于发烧，而是基于嗅觉能力。

sentences.en: Hopkins, who partnered with scientists from Belgium, Italy, and elsewhere to publish more

sentences.en: smell training and other as yet unknown treatments for people who have lost their sense of smell.
sentences.zh: 嗅觉训练以及其他尚未发现的针对嗅觉丧失者的治疗方法的研究。

sentences.en: It's a problem that she thinks will be taken much more seriously in a post-COVID world in which many people, possibly millions of them, never fully recover their olfaction.
sentences.zh: 她认为，在一个后新冠时代，这个问题会得到更认真的对待，因为许多人，可能多达数百万人，永远无法完全恢复嗅觉。

sentences.en: If smell was ignored before, off in the hinterlands, you could say that COVID put it on the map.
sentences.zh: 如果说嗅觉以前被忽视，处于边缘地带，那么可以说新冠疫情让它受到了重视。

sentences.en: But studying smell, scientist after scientist told me, had already reshaped the way they thought about the world and their place in it.
sentences.zh: 但科学家们纷纷告诉我，研究嗅觉已经重塑了他们对世界以及他们在其中所处位置的看法。

sentences.en: They went, they said, from thinking of smell as a bonus sense to a dominant one.
sentences.zh: 他们说，他们从认为嗅觉是一种额外感官转变为认为它是一种主导感官。

sentences.en: And from a secondary sense to one of the primary things that influences our life.
sentences.zh: 并从一种次要感官转变为影响我们生活的主要事物之一。

sentences.zh: 即使在他们努力绘制地图的过程中，地理位置也已经发生了变化。
